inferred_requirements.title: ARINC 429 Bus Frame Ingestion
inferred_requirements.description: The system shall continuously ingest and buffer ARINC 429 bus frames from connected avionics sensors and line-replaceable units.
inferred_requirements.justification: Directly stated requirement in the user prompt to handle ARINC 429 bus frames.

inferred_requirements.title: Solid-State Crash-Survivable Memory Flush on Power Loss
inferred_requirements.description: Upon detection of primary aircraft power loss, the system shall execute an emergency flush of the buffered ARINC 429 frames to solid-state crash-survivable memory.
inferred_requirements.justification: Directly stated core function of flushing data to crash-survivable memory during power loss.

inferred_requirements.title: Hold-Up Capacitor Energy Reserve
inferred_requirements.description: The hardware subsystem shall incorporate a dedicated hold-up energy storage mechanism (e.g., capacitor bank) to maintain sufficient operational voltage during power interruption for the duration of the memory flush sequence.
inferred_requirements.justification: Why 1 (Problem/Context): Writing data to solid-state memory requires active power, but primary aircraft power is lost. Why 2 (Technical Mechanism): An auxiliary energy hold-up circuit must power the volatile memory buffers and non-volatile write controllers until the flush completes. Why 3 (Mandatory Invariant): The system must never experience a brownout-induced memory corruption before the entire buffer queue is successfully committed.

inferred_requirements.title: Atomic Ring Buffer Write Operations
inferred_requirements.description: The flight data recorder software shall utilize lock-free atomic ring buffers for ARINC 429 frame ingestion to prevent race conditions and priority inversions between the data acquisition loop and the power-fail interrupt handler.
inferred_requirements.justification: Why 1 (Problem/Context): Interrupt-driven power loss handlers can trigger while the main thread is writing to the buffer, leading to partial writes or data corruption. Why 2 (Technical Mechanism): Lock-free atomic head/tail pointer management ensures memory consistency without blocking real-time execution. Why 3 (Mandatory Invariant): The buffer state must remain deterministic and fully readable down to the exact clock cycle of power failure.

inferred_requirements.title: ED-112 / TSO-C123 Compliance Architecture
inferred_requirements.description: The crash-survivable memory module and associated buffer synchronization firmware shall be designed to comply with rigorous structural and environmental survivability standards applicable to flight data recorder systems.
inferred_requirements.justification: Crash-survivable memory architectures inherently operate under strict airworthiness and survivability standards such as EUROCAE ED-112 or FAA TSO-C123.

inferred_requirements.title: Solid-State Memory Interface Protocol
inferred_requirements.description: The specific physical interface protocol, controller model, and low-level block write command structure for the solid-state crash-survivable memory are unstated.
inferred_requirements.justification: The prompt references 'solid-state crash-survivable memory' generally, but does not specify proprietary hardware interfaces, NAND flash protocols, or specific memory manufacturer datasheets.

inferred_requirements.title: Power Loss Detection Threshold and Hardware Signal
inferred_requirements.description: The exact hardware sensing mechanism, voltage drop trip point, and interrupt line used to signal primary power loss to the processor are unstated.
inferred_requirements.justification: The prompt mandates flushing 'on power loss' but does not specify the precise hardware sensor topology (e.g., discrete analog comparator threshold, power supply health pin interrupt).
